{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUDROfM8AAAABd0A4hw", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlR_zzhHVLbg", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlR_z", "number": 253, "title": "Separate Graph Library management from launch settings and remove use-case-specific graph UI", "body": "## Problem

The master/detail Graph Library redesign in #250 improved navigation, but the library still presents graphs as if they are inherently tied to two particular product uses:

- `Use this graph for` / `Use for Live` / `Use for Web voice typing` controls sit **inside the selected graph detail**.
- The graph list displays `Live` and `Web voice typing` assignment tags on entries.
- A global `Web voice typing` switch sits outside the graph list, yet assignment is in the details. It is easy to confuse **graph selection**, **launch binding** and **feature enablement**.

Graphs are general-purpose pipelines (ASR, translation, summarization, audio synthesis, etc.), not "voice-typing graphs" by nature. Launch options are properties of **entry points / UI triggers** that consume a saved graph, not attributes or management actions on the graph itself.

## Requested UX / information architecture

**Keep Graph Library focused on creating, finding, viewing, editing and managing graphs. Put the bindings and opt-in for launching them in a distinct compact `Launch settings` section below the library master/detail area.**

Conceptual layout:

```text
Graph Library                                      [+ New graph]
[ Search… ] [sort/filter]

┌──────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Graphs                   │ Selected graph                     │
│                          │                                    │
│ Voice Input              │ Voice Input                        │
│ Meeting Notes            │ [graph preview]                    │
│ Translation              │ [Edit graph] [Duplicate] [⋯]       │
│ ...                      │ [Name] [Description] [Save details]│
│                          │ [metadata/recovery when needed]    │
└──────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────┘

Launch settings
┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Live window                  [Meeting Notes        ▾]         │
│ Web page microphone button   [Voice Input          ▾]   [ON]  │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

The intent is that a user can identify **what they are configuring (the launch surface)** without understanding “default execution targets,” “use this graph for,” or other implementation vocabulary.

### Graph Library area (management only)

- Remove the `Use this graph for` section and its `Use for Live`, `Use for Web voice typing`, `Unassign` controls from the selected graph detail.
- Remove use-specific `Live` / `Web voice typing` markers from ordinary list rows so the list presents **graphs, not their current application**.
- Preserve the #250 left-list/right-detail layout, selection, preview, rename/description, `Edit graph`, `Duplicate`, `⋯` (Export/Delete/Check model files), search, sort, filter, error/recovery workflows.
- No assignment changes should happen when merely selecting a graph. If a graph cannot be deleted because a launch setting references it, show a compact actionable reason like `Used by a launch setting; choose another graph in Launch settings first.`

### Separate Launch settings area (entry points, not graph properties)

- Title: **`Launch settings`** (or a similarly concise user-facing name, not `Default execution targets`).
- One clear row per **launch surface**:
  1. **`Live window`** — dropdown chooses the saved graph used for the next Live session.
  2. **`Web page microphone button`** — dropdown chooses the saved graph for the mic-button invocation, with a distinct **ON/OFF switch** controlling website mic UI. Avoid `Web voice typing` as the organizing concept; use words that describe **where/how the user launches a graph**.
- The dropdowns and ON/OFF must be visually and semantically distinct: a graph being chosen does **not** enable microphone injection or grant website permission. ON/OFF must not silently change the saved assignment. Default OFF for new/upgrade users stays as-is.
- Show graph names in dropdowns; display `Not assigned` only for the Web mic trigger when none is bound. The Live window always has one valid default. Incompatible graphs are disabled or rejected with a short, actionable explanation (`webVoiceError` and `usable`), never replaced silently with the Live default.
- Assignment changes apply to the **next** session. Running sessions retain their graph snapshot. Changing the selected item in the library does not change an entry-point binding.
- Keep the launch section compact, aligned and responsive; don't let long instructional copy dominate. Use layout/proximity and simple names first. Just-in-time permission rationale/explicit browser permission request and context-sensitive error/recovery stay intact, with a small optional info/help disclosure when needed.
- Future entry points (keyboard shortcuts, context menu, etc.) should fit the same section as additional rows, **not** require adding purpose-specific controls to each graph detail. No need to implement future entry points or a general plugin/framework architecture here.

## Important implementation constraints

- **UI-only information architecture change.** Reuse existing `GraphLibrary.assignments.live` and `assignments.webVoice`, the `GraphLibrary.assign()` validated/locked revision-aware mutation path, `webVoiceError` eligibility, and the separately persisted `chrome.storage.local` Web voice preference.
- No changes to graph JSON schema/version, stable IDs, graph runtime semantics, model loading, inference, host permission scope, opt-in defaults or Chrome content script injection policy.
- Preserve conflict handling and cross-tab updates: changing a binding in another Library tab should update the selector and not discard unsaved graph name/description edits. Handle stale revisions/failed writes with actionable errors and no false success.
- Preserve the permission and security UX from #247/#250: permission is requested **only after explicit ON**, consent reason is shown at the point of enablement, denial leaves OFF, and OFF removes controls/stops capture. Correctly re-enable only when a compatible graph is bound.
- Keep clear access for keyboard users and screen readers: actual `label`–`select` association, accessible switch name/state, meaningful focus after errors; do not rely on spatial layout alone for accessible meaning.
- Prefer existing CSS patterns and no unrelated Graph Editor / Live or mic-icon visual redesign (#249 is separate).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Selected graph details contain only graph management, preview, metadata and graph-edit actions; **no `Use this graph for`** or purpose-specific assignment buttons.
- [ ] Ordinary graph list rows no longer display use-specific Live/Web voice tags. Selecting a graph changes details only.
- [ ] A distinct, concise **Launch settings** section sits outside/below Graph Library master/detail, with `Live window` and `Web page microphone button` rows and their graph selectors.
- [ ] The Web mic row has an independent ON/OFF switch; assignment, consent and active recording states are not conflated. The default-off rule still holds.
- [ ] Saving a Live selection changes `assignments.live`; selecting an eligible Web mic graph changes `assignments.webVoice`; unassignment is possible only where supported. Saved names/IDs survive rename/reorder/reload.
- [ ] Invalid/ineligible graphs cannot be launched for that surface; the UI gives a succinct reason without fallback to another graph. A bound graph cannot be deleted until reassigned/unassigned.
- [ ] Website permission flow, ongoing session snapshot, stop/revoke behavior, model caching and running Live / in-page voice use are unchanged.
- [ ] No long permanent explanatory paragraphs; just-in-time permission rationale and important errors remain available and accessible.
- [ ] Responsive/mobile-width and keyboard/assistive technology behavior tested; navigation and focus remain obvious.
- [ ] Update Graph Library UI/E2E tests to exercise both selectors, on/off gating, cross-tab updates, invalid graphs, stale revisions and safe graph deletion; update docs/screenshots where applicable, record tests actually run.

## Context

Follows #243 (multi-graph library), #247 (opt-in in-page mic execution), and #250 (master/detail UI).

This task specifically **separates management of generic pipelines from configuration of their launch entry points**. Do not modify graph execution behavior or implement site-specific X/Twitter rich-text insertion changes.
